title: Nancy J. Plowman v. Philadelphia Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal sustained on all three issues: (1) Presbytery erred in ruling that the LVPC Session could resume the trial with a new TE moderator chosen by the Session; (2) Presbytery erred in not lifting all suspensions of Mrs. Plowman from the Lord's Table; (3) Presbytery erred in finding no manifestation of prejudice. The SJC set aside all judgments and censures and found no reasonable possibility of a fair and unbiased trial on this or any similarly related matter. It held the November 13, 2003 communion communication was not a formal censure but pious advice, so Presbytery did not have to act on it.
first_summary: The SJC sustained Nancy Plowman's appeal from Philadelphia Presbytery, holding that Presbytery erred by allowing the Lehigh Valley Session to resume her trial and by not lifting all suspensions from the Lord's Table. It set aside all judgments and censures and remanded for a new trial under a different moderator.
summary: A member suspended from the Lord's Table appealed after Presbytery let the Session resume her trial and failed to lift all suspensions. The SJC sustained the appeal, finding the Session's premature censure, truncated trial, and prosecutor-judge conflict manifested prejudice and made a fair trial impossible. It set aside all judgments and censures, treated the November 13, 2003 communion letter as non-censuring advice, and did not remand.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2004-02, Nancy J. Plowman v. Philadelphia Presbytery; SJC decision adopted at lines 153-157 (21 concurring, 0 dissenting, 1 recused, 2 absent). Source: cases/ga33_2005__2004-02.md, sha256 0a4247a67d25238ba54ccc8a694e4d34e085e9731c8e876e927cb71e1b5e261a.
evidence_notes.dispute: LVPC Session suspended Plowman from the Lord's Table on Dec. 21, 2001 without due process; after a trial ended in contumacy and indefinite suspension on July 1, 2002, Presbytery's Jan. 10, 2004 decision reversed contumacy and lifted the July 1 censure but allowed the Session to resume trial and did not lift all suspensions (lines 17-41, 47-51).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC answered all three issues Yes and sustained the appeal (lines 53-59). It found manifest prejudice from the premature censure without due process, failure to lift the suspension, truncated trial before her evidence, and TE Stone's roles as judge, prosecutor, and witness; no fair trial was possible on this or related matters (lines 63-121). All judgments and censures were set aside.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The Nov. 13, 2003 Session letter did not formally invoke suspension but was pious advice under BCO 36-5; Presbytery did not have to act on it (lines 123-151). The SJC distinguished the two earlier suspensions from that letter. Panel: TE Bob Stuart, RE John White, TE Steven Meyerhoff (line 153).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Prior SJC Oct. 16, 2003 decision remanded the case to Presbytery to hear the July 31, 2002 appeal (line 33); Presbytery's Jan. 10, 2004 decision is quoted at lines 35-40. The current decision sets aside all judgments and censures.
